From that point onward, players can construct ships through dispatch missions or buy them from fleetmasters, customize them with purchased parts, and undertake maritime trading with newly added goods . Uncharted islands offer new missions, while treasure maps point toward hidden rewards throughout the world.

Below the surface, diving introduces a breath gauge, and your maximum capacity increases as you refine your diving suit. New equipment allows the A.T.A.G (All-Terrain Armored Gear, Crimson Desert's pilotable mech ) to operate underwater, and underwater creatures can become registered mounts after players raise their Trust by subduing or feeding them , depending on their type. Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane also receive one individual quest each, available after completing the main story quest titled Journey's End.

Marriage, Housing, and Businesses

The expansion's housing overhaul lets players design layouts and place structural elements, including walls and windows. There are 17 additional residences and two castles to decorate , while liberated strongholds can accommodate restaurants, sawmills, smithies, and tailor’s shops that continue operating while you are away.

Relationships receive an additional Trust level, with flirting, gifts, and conversations eventually allowing a marriage proposal at 100 Trust . Spouses can live in a designated residence, accompany players on their travels, and occasionally provide gifts. Camp festivals offer another way to build relationships and recruit certain visitors as Honorary Greymanes for dispatch missions.

For combat-focused players, the Garden of Trials introduces ten challenge groups after Journey’s End . You can bring up to three playable characters, determine their battle order, and continue with the next character when one falls. Food-based healing is disabled for this gauntlet, though clearing each group enhances an existing skill. New bosses and equipment round out the combat-related additions.

Finally, PC players gain independently selectable upscaling and frame-generation technologies , including the option to combine DLSS upscaling with FSR Frame Generation. Pearl Abyss did share one important warning: saves created with the DLC installed cannot be loaded or cross-saved into a version without it.

The developer did not share review codes ahead of the DLC's debut, so it might be a while before you see our review. Meanwhile, are you planning to get back into Crimson Desert with Charting the Unknown (which is priced at $24.99 )? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Director Insisted It Isn’t a “Soulslike”, but Day One PC Mods Add FromSoftware’s Enemy Respawns and Boss Resets
item.description:
Following the announcement of Phantom Blade Zero , director Soulframe Liang made abundantly clear that S-Game 's first AAA game on PC and PlayStation 5 isn't a soulslike , as it doesn't feature some of FromSoftware 's most brutal gameplay mechanics, such as enemies respawning every time a checkpoint is activated or multi-phase bosses reverting to phase one if the player is defeated. While this may be disappointing for some, on PC , some day one mods bring these mechanics into the game, ultimately making its great combat mechanics that were worth a perfect score in my opinion, and the experience generally more challenging.

Enemy Respawn

The Bellbound-Enemies Respawn mod does exactly what its name implies: it makes enemies respawn when Soul rings a checkpoint bell to rest or when he is defeated. "Does the world of Wulin feel too empty? Bellbound: Enemies Respawn brings ordinary enemies back to life when you use a bell, fast travel, or die and revive, keeping the world populated for exploration and repeat combat," the mod's description reads on Nexus Mods .

To add more tension to the experience, the mod's current version also forces a 23% Phantom Dust loss upon defeat, which can be further increased or decreased in the mod's configuration file. This is a great idea, as defeat in Phantom Blade Zero doesn't carry any major penalty outside of getting sent back to the last checkpoint.

As I highlighted in my review, I really wished enemy respawn was a thing in the vanilla game as it would have provided more opportunities to experiment with the game's weapons, so I immediately downloaded this mod as soon as it became available. In my current playthrough in 66-Days mode , the mod is working as intended, and with version 1.4 enemies near checkpoint bells no longer respawn, which was an issue in previous versions.

Boss Phase Reset

Similarly, the Boss Phase Reset mod brings another one of FromSoftware 's signature mechanics to Phantom Blade Zero . "In Phantom Blade Zero, when you beat a boss's first phase and then die, you come back at the start of the second phase. This mod takes that checkpoint away: die in phase 2 (or 3, or later) and the next attempt starts at phase 1, like a classic boss fight. You have to beat every phase again in one go," reads the mod's description on Nexus Mods . This is achieved in a rather clever way by having an autosave stored the moment the boss fight begins, which gets loaded when the player is defeated, thus reverting the battle to phase 1 by disabling any saving during phase 2.

While I did test this mod, I uninstalled it after confirming it was working properly in an older save file I had in Hellwalker mode . 66-Days mode is brutal with the limited amount of lives Soul has, and as bosses are challenging, I felt having battles reset to phase 1 every time would have made this difficulty mode more frustrating than challenging, even with upgraded endgame weapons. However, those who want to test their skills to the extreme will find plenty of use for this mod.

Devil May Cry-style Combat Ranks

Interestingly enough, FromSoftware 's brutal gameplay mechanics aren't the only mechanics from another iconic Japanese developer to get brought over to Phantom Blade Zero with a mod. "Phantom Blade Zero's combat is built for flair: perfect deflects, perfect dodges, executions, Sha-Chi arts. Style Rank scores it. Fight with variety and skill and your rank climbs from D to SSS in the game's own brush lettering; stand around, spam one move or get hit and it falls. When the fight ends, a grade card tells you how you did," reads the Style Rank mod's description on Nexus Mods . While there's no reward for a good performance, it adds an interesting layer to the combat mechanics that Devil May Cry and character action fans will surely appreciate.

While I somehow expected Phantom Blade Zero 's modding scene to be vibrant, I never expected to see so many interesting mods released only a little over 24 hours after the game's launch. As such, I am really excited to see what's in store for the future of what I believe to be one of the best action role-playing games of the generation.

item.title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan Breaks Silence On Quantum Computing Acquisition & Says Intel Will Become A Full Stack Revenue-Generating Quantum Company”
item.description:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan believes that the total addressable market for his firm's CPUs, when it comes to demand stemming from the AI agentic market, could surge to $200 billion over five years. The executive made the remarks during Intel's latest earnings call, where he reiterated the advantages of using CPUs in AI computing. Tan, whose firm also recently bought quantum computing firm Classiq, shared that the deal will enable Intel to become a "full stack revenue-generating" quantum computing company.

Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan Touts Power Efficiency Advantages Of CPUs Over GPUs When It Comes To AI Computing

Tan's remarks for CPUs and agentic AI come after the Intel CEO described how he uses the technology. In Late last month, the Intel CEO outlined that he uses agentic AI to do his "homework" by running the AI agents overnight and relying on their output in the morning.

During Intel's third quarter earrings call, Tan continued to assert that the demand for CPUs in agentic AI computing will prove beneficial for Intel. Remarking that CPUs are more efficient, Tan shared that with energy efficiency being more important for the AI buildout, "deterministic CPU are far more efficient at doing tasks" when compared to GPUs being great at "thinking tasks."

He added:

"While GPU reasoning query run as high as multiple watt-hours of energy, a single CPU query could cost only joules of energy."

The Intel CEO, not known for brashly expressing strong optimism, is nevertheless quite optimistic about the future of CPUs for agentic AI applications. He discussed the total addressable market and outlined:

"Applying even conservative estimates to the total number of digital agents and agents served per CPU, it is easy to anticipate a massive dollar and unit TAM for CPUs over the coming five years. By our estimates, server CPU TAM, largely driven by agentic workloads, could increase as much as five times from where it is today, from $40 billion to more than $200 billion over five years. This makes the opportunity for Intel enormous."

Tan also discussed Intel's recent acquisition of the quantum computing firm Classiq. The Intel CEO discussed Classiq in September, noting its position in the software sector of the quantum computing industry.

Back then, Tan had r emarked that the firm had clear visibility into market visibility as part of a broader set of remarks that had asserted that quantum computing's viability depended on market conditions. Classiq's integration of classical and quantum computing had also impressed the Intel executive.

Naturally, with commercialization being paramount for Tan, in his latest remarks about Classiq, he praised the firm's "overarching hardware-agnostic software platform layer provides a gateway for more consumers to explore quantum computing."

Tan has high hopes from the acquisition and even believes that it will allow Intel to become a revenue-generating quantum computing company:

"It is a wonderful complement to our already strong internal quantum hardware and software stacks and enable us to further extend our compute platform offerings to include QPUs in addition to CPUs, GPUs, and ASICs. Post-acquisition, Intel will become a full stack revenue-generating quantum computing company."

item.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma Pointed to Record Minecraft and World of Warcraft Forever Sales, but Circana Sees No Impact From Her Initiatives
item.description:
Following Xbox 's continued revenue decline this past quarter , CEO Asha Sharma tried to focus on the positives (like record sales of Minecraft and World of Warcraft Forever ), but Circana analyst Mat Piscatella has painted a rather troubling picture of Sharma's sweeping initiatives: they're having very little impact . Speaking on the latest episode of Christopher Dring's The Game Business Show , he said:

With Xbox and everything they’re doing, all of the new programs they’re putting into place... At least in the sales and engagement data that I look at, I’m not seeing that have any positive impact . The disc-to-digital program hasn’t changed their sales of new physical software trend at all. No matter what they do in terms of the console side, saying Gears is going to be exclusive, that hasn’t made any difference in terms of the hardware trend. In fact, the hardware trend keeps getting worse. They’ve lost some distribution in the US. So it just seems like everything they’re doing is not having a positive impact.

I don’t know what they do. It’s really hard to find any signs of positivity or hope on that platform right now . Everything they’re doing seems to be getting Twitter likes from the most passionate part of their fan base, but other than that, in terms of the actual results, I’m not seeing anything right now. And I’m looking really hard. Gears is beautiful. It is a gorgeous game, but you make it exclusive, kind of chop the legs out from under its potential as an individual title in order to try to boost your platform, and at least in the short term, it hasn’t made a difference .

Moreover, according to Piscatella, even the big business decision to remove Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (and future installments, too) from Game Pass at launch to boost full-price sales has seemingly failed .

Last year, with the Game Pass day-one launch, according to our US engagement tracker or worldwide engagement tracker data for Xbox, we had about 28% of players last year on Xbox who turned on their Xbox on that day and played Call of Duty. So, a good chunk, right? This year, on the same day the game was fully released, that was 14%. So that engagement rate was cut in half because the game wasn’t available on Game Pass on day one.

We’ve seen this dramatic downtick in terms of the daily engagement rate on Call of Duty on Xbox because it isn’t on the subscription service, and we didn’t see a whole bunch of Xbox players buy the game this year because it wasn’t available. Maybe there’s a gap there because still 14% of people played. So you had some gap there. But it wasn’t like they maintained the player count. All the people who played on Game Pass last year went out and bought it this year—that just doesn’t look like that was the case at all.

So, what did it buy you? All this really does is you’ve hurt the value proposition of the one key differentiator of your platform: Game Pass. So you’ve removed some of that value proposition there. You haven’t improved the value proposition anywhere else, and you’ve raised the price significantly a couple of times. That’s a bad combination, especially leading into a holiday.

There is one important caveat: Piscatella acknowledged that he did not yet have the sales data needed to establish whether more players bought Call of Duty outright this year. The drop in engagement is clear, but the financial payoff of removing it from Game Pass remains an open question. Even so, his broader criticism is difficult to dismiss: Xbox has weakened a key subscription benefit without a visible improvement in its console and game sales .

Sharma, for her part, maintains that console sales are constrained by supply issues, while Microsoft expects content and services revenue to return to growth next quarter. Those are different measures from the engagement and hardware trends Piscatella is highlighting here, but together they underline the challenge ahead: a stronger publishing business does not automatically translate into a healthier Xbox console ecosystem, and, for now, the promised turnaround remains unproven .

item.title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan Says Nova Lake Will Fill The High-End Client CPU Gap, Coral Rapids “14A” To Be Competitive Against AMD & Next-Gen To Take The Lead Over EPYC
item.description:
Intel is betting its success in the client and data center spectrums on the next-generation Nova Lake and Coral Rapids CPUs.

Intel Nova Lake Fills An Important Hole In Its Client CPU Gap, A Market That AMD Has Captured Tremendously In Recent Years

It is interesting that besides leaks, the only official way Intel has disclosed its next-gen client & data center CPU lineups has been during investor/earnings calls. While we know a lot about the Nova Lake and Diamond Rapids families today, a year ago, Intel did talk about them but only in these calls. Diamond Rapids did see a good presentation during Hot Chips, but despite being called a savior of its client desktop segment, the company has yet to talk about Nova Lake in the various events it has hosted so far this year.

Now it makes sense why Intel has avoided talking about Nova Lake because they were focusing on Panther Lake and a refreshed Arrow Lake lineup for desktops, but we all know how consumers have responded to Arrow Lake "Core Ultra 200S" in general. The new "Plus" SKUs do offer good value, but they are designed for a platform that has hit a dead end, and Nova Lake itself will be launching on a brand new socket which is expected to offer much better multi-generational CPU support than its predecessors.

So during its Q3 2026 earnings call, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan reaffirmed that Nova Lake "Core Ultra Series 4" will be their first 18A-P product for the client segment. We know that the compute tile is not the one using this node. Intel did use 18A-P to evaluate early samples , but the chips were always going to use TSMC's N2P node, the same as AMD's next-gen Ryzen "Olympic Ridge" CPUs.

Intel's client segment took a massive hit during Q3 2026 due to memory shortages and increasing prices. The company has already warned of further declines in the coming quarters, and with the DRAM segment being worse in 2027 than it is in 2026, there is little hope that the consumer PC segment is going to do any better.

But with all that said, Intel says that it is "Enthusiastic" with its Nova Lake launch, and is expecting twice as many design wins as Panther Lake at launch.

Nova Lake, our first Intel 18A-P client product, is tracking ahead of schedule, with design wins expecting to be twice those of Panther Lake at launch. We look forward to sharing more at CES in January. As the market normalizes, we expect this portfolio drives meaningful share gains.

Lip-Bu Tan - Intel CEO (Q3 2026 Earnings Call)

Intel is making a lot of bets with Nova Lake, a fully top-to-bottom lineup that will span from high-end desktops to mainstream laptops. The company expects Nova Lake to be a main driver for its market share once the market normalizes.

And it is finally giving us a launch timeframe. CES 2027 in January is said to be the place where we will learn more about Nova Lake CPUs, and it looks like this will be the official unveiling followed by a formal launch. Do note that Nova Lake will launch in multiple phases on desktops, with the single compute tile (up to 28-core SKUs) launching first, followed by dual compute tile models in the latter part of 2027 (up to 52-core SKUs) . These chips will feature a new BFC cache solution to tackle AMD's Ryzen X3D chips.

With Nova Lake, Intel plans to fill in the hole in its portfolio for high-end desktops. As mentioned above, Core Ultra 200S failed to do that against AMD's Ryzen 9000 chips, and Intel wants to once again redeem itself in this space with better options for content creators, ultra-enthusiasts, and more.

The one added piece of this is we come into next year with Nova Lake as our product offering. We think this is the best set of products we've had in a very long time. We think it covers the gamut of what's required to participate in client. We're very excited about it.

You know, as we go into next year, you know, we'll have Nova Lake, and I think the important aspect of Nova Lake is, you know, we've had a bit of a hole in our portfolio for high-end desktop, and Nova Lake filled in that gap.

Lip-Bu Tan - Intel CEO (Q3 2026 Earnings Call)

Besides the client side, Intel also shed some light on its Xeon side of things, which will play a pivotal role in the company's future, primarily the AI side of things. The DCAI side has done well, but supply constraints have really hampered its full potential. Intel also faces pressure from a growing list of competition from Arm solutions such as NVIDIA's Vera, Arm's AGI, and its age-old rival in the x86 segment, AMD.

AMD's EPYC Venice CPUs are already ramping while Intel is yet to release its Diamond Rapids CPUs. With up to 256 P-Cores, Diamond Rapids launching in 2027 will have a lot of competition to face.

Intel once again highlights that it expects its Coral Rapids Xeon CPUs, the generation succeeding Diamond Rapids, to be competitive against AMD's EPYC family while using the 14A process node , and to take the lead against AMD EPYC with future tick-tock Xeon chips.

Now we've been hearing a lot from Intel about its Xeon CPUs rivaling AMD EPYC, but generations later, the company has yet to offer solid solutions, only being seen as the 2nd-tier solution on the market. This led Intel to reverse course on some decisions made by former CEO Pat Gelsinger, such as the removal of SMT, which comes back with Coral Rapids .

And then we are in the shipping in revenue that's on 18A. We should have capacity for that. And then Diamond Rapids, that will be 2027.We have 18A-P will be ready for that. And of course, the Coral Rapids coming up in 2028, that will be on the 14A. So those, I think, will be in pretty good shape.

So clearly we have a roadmap. We like what we have in terms of Coral Rapids will be competitive to AMD. And then next, next general product, the Tick-Tock will be ahead of the AMD on that.

Lip-Bu Tan - Intel CEO (Q3 2026 Earnings Call)

Despite near-term headwinds from memory shortages that have pressured client volumes, the company remains highly confident in the platform’s design-win momentum and its ability to drive meaningful share gains once the market normalizes.

We think next year and in the future years, we're in a market share gain type of environment for our client. Obviously, unfortunate that we've run into this challenge on the memory side and its impact on client, but we are very enthusiastic about the product side. You didn't ask this question, but I'll just extend it out beyond this year.

We do think that the PC is going to go through a renaissance despite this. We think that as AI workloads start to shift around, there's going to be a lot of workload required in the client space, either as a PC or as some kind of agentic box. We do see this market as being pretty interesting.

Lip-Bu Tan - Intel CEO (Q3 2026 Earnings Call)

On the data-center side, the succession from Diamond Rapids to Coral Rapids (on the 14A node) is positioned as the point where Intel expects to close the competitiveness gap with AMD’s EPYC lineup while restoring features such as SMT, setting the stage for subsequent generations to pull ahead. Taken together, these efforts reflect a measured bet that stronger product fundamentals, coupled with a longer-term “PC renaissance” fueled by shifting AI workloads, can translate into sustained market-share recovery across both client and server segments.

item.title: NVIDIA’s RTX 5080 24 GB Could Arrive As Early As December With 50% More VRAM, As 16 GB Models Already Sell For Over $2,000

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB Is Launching At A Time When GPU Prices Are Blowing Through The Roof

item.title: TSMC Co-COO Y.P. Chyn Says Longer Hours Don’t Improve R&D, Recalling The Company’s 24-Hour “Night Owl” Program That Failed In Just 6 Months
item.description:
During a conversation with students at National Cheng Kung University, as part of the United Daily News Group’s “United 75, Smart Future” event series, TSMC Co-COO and Executive Vice President Y.P. Chyn revealed that the company once tried running its R&D around the clock under a program called “Night Owl,” only to scrap it after just six months. The program dates back to a period when TSMC was behind on process technology and was racing to catch up with its global competitors.

Chyn says that R&D runs on brainpower, not labor, and that working longer hours won’t necessarily produce desired results

The report from Economic Daily News states that, according to Chyn, a theory emerged at the time that if TSMC’s R&D team worked 24 hours a day while U.S. competitors worked only eight, the company could gain a time advantage and overtake them. To put the idea into practice, TSMC encouraged R&D engineers to take on night-time development work, hoping that longer operating hours would speed up progress. The plan didn’t hold up, and it was declared a failure within half a year.

Chyn said the experience taught the company a lasting lesson, which is that R&D depends on thinking, judgment, and innovation, and cannot be improved simply by adding more working hours. He summed it up by saying that R&D runs on brainpower, not labor. The Co-COO also described the 40nm node as a major turning point for TSMC’s organization.

At the time, the traditional model of the R&D department finishing a process and then handing it over to the fabrication plants ran into serious setbacks, forcing the company to rethink how its research and manufacturing teams should work together. That reassessment gradually gave rise to what TSMC calls its “One Team” culture, which Chyn credits as a key factor in pushing its technology to the top of the industry.

According to Chyn, One Team is not just about asking employees to support one another. It means giving different departments a shared goal and making them jointly accountable for the final result. He offered two examples of how this works in practice. When a new process moves from R&D to volume production, a longer overlap period, with the fab involved early in development, makes the ramp much smoother.

Alternatively, when a fab runs into a process problem, bringing multiple teams together to analyze the root cause can resolve it far faster than leaving it to a single unit to isolate the problem. The same philosophy extends to TSMC’s global expansion. Chyn said overseas fabs cannot operate as organizations fully separated from Taiwan, and that Taiwanese teams must work closely with their overseas counterparts and take some responsibility for their success.

Assuming this process is adopted, it’ll result in smoother technology transfer and overseas operations. Chyn has admitted that getting departments to genuinely embrace One Team takes a great deal of time and effort, and that it can’t be achieved through slogans alone. Still, he believes cross-department collaboration has improved both process development and mass production efficiency, and that it remains a core foundation of TSMC’s technology leadership.

News Source: Economic Daily News

item.title: Intel’s Data Center Business Is Now Almost As Big As Its PC Division After A 78% Surge, While Q4 Guidance Hints At Softer Revenue And Thinner Margins
item.description:
The Q3 2026 financial results from Intel are here, with the company posting revenue of $16.5 billion, which is up 21 percent from $13.7 billion a year earlier. The company’s standout performer was the Data Center and AI (DCAI) group, which posted $7.3 billion in revenue, resulting in a 78 percent jump year-over-year. Despite operating income for the segment more than tripling to $3.04 billion from $964 million, not every segment from Intel has a happy ending. In fact, the PC segment has a grim tale, as we dive deeper into the figures.

CFO David Zinsner stated that Intel’s Q3 2026 results were the company’s strongest data center growth in 15 years, but the PC category slipped 5 percent

CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company’s immediate priority is unlocking more supply to meet what he described as extraordinary demand for Xeon, with Intel’s CFO David Zinsner also commenting on the remarkable performance from the data center side. Unfortunately, that’s where the positive news ends, as the Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) saw the complete opposite of the DCAI group.

CCPG brought in $8.1 billion, down 5 percent, with operating income slipping to $2.29 billion from $2.69 billion. Zinsner has sounded alarm bells, stating that the PC slowdown is expected to continue at least through the first half of next year, and Intel’s risk disclosures point to industry-wide substrate and memory shortages as a lingering concern. As for the foundry business, it generated $6.7 billion in revenue, up 58 percent when including internal sales, though it still posted an operating loss of $1.85 billion.

Still, the silver lining is that it’s an improvement on the $2.32 billion loss from the same quarter last year. During the Q3 2026 quarter, Intel released the 14A 0.9 process design kit and announced collaborations with ASML on High-NA EUV , along with Lam Research and Applied Materials on new capacity and joint R&D. Profitability improved sharply on an underlying basis, with Intel’s non-GAAP gross margin rising to 44.1 percent from 40.0 percent, and non-GAAP operating margin climbing to 19.6 percent from 11.2 percent.

The fourth-quarter outlook is where investors may see some caution. After all, Intel is guiding revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, which is below the Q3 2026 level, with non-GAAP gross margin falling to around 38 percent, roughly half of this quarter’s result. During the earnings announcement, Intel doesn’t explain the Q4 margin decline, and it gives no segment-level guidance.

The closest context that we could determine was Zinsner’s comment regarding the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year, and Tan’s focus on unlocking Xeon supply. Any explanation for the margin drop, such as product mix, ramp costs, or memory pricing, we’ll learn in future updates, so it’s best that readers remain patient for our future analysis.

item.title: Sir Patrick Stewart dies aged 86
item.description:
Actor and philanthropist, Sir Patrick Stewart, died on Wednesday, the 28th of October, aged 86, in his home, after suffering from Alzheimers Diesease and Lewy Body Dementia.

His family posted a statement on the 29th on X, announcing his passing.

We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” wrote family spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.

Born in Mirfield, just 30 minutes from where I live, in 1940, Sir Patrick Stewart has a list of roles spanning the spectrum, including Robin Hood: Men in Tights, Dune, Moby-Dick, TNMT, The Green Room, Hamlet, American Dad, and so much more.

In theatre, there isn't a role he hasn't touched as a classic Shakespearean, having played King Claudius, Macbeth, Prospero, Mark Anthony, and Othello. Other plays featuring the actor have taken both the West End and Broadway by storm.

Of course, the roles people will remember him for are two of the biggest: Captain Jean-Luc Picard, and Professor Charles Xavier. For me, it was as Jean-Luc, as I grew up watching him as the authoritative yet compassionate and caring Captain Jean-Luc Picard, and then seeing him as an equally compassionate but incredibly powerful Professor Charles Xavier, particularly in one of the best pieces of acting I've ever seen in Logan.

As a gamer, it's impossible not to remember his brief but commanding role as Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion , as Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, or as the narrator in titles like Felix the Reaper or The Sims: Medieval. He also voiced Jean-Luc and Charles Xavier many times in various Star Trek and X-Men titles.

In lieu of flowers, the family has asked that memorial contributions be made to Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund or Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources .

Also, if you're British, watch this. Hell, watch it even if you aren't, because it matters - and it will give you a much-needed laugh at the end, after the bad news.
